user.title: Terrazzo
user.description: Adds a Terrazzo dashboard to the sidebar at /terrazzo. It draws your Lovelace dashboards and signs in as whoever opens it.

data_description.title: The name of the /terrazzo panel in the sidebar.
data_description.dashboard: Leave empty to start on the dashboard picker. Any dashboard can still be opened from the panel, or bookmarked as /terrazzo?dashboard= followed by its URL path.
data_description.top_level_dashboards: Show Lovelace dashboards directly in the sidebar as Terrazzo panels (/terrazzo-<slug>) and hide the generic Terrazzo link. Choose "Hidden Lovelace dashboards" to automatically promote dashboards whose "Show in sidebar" toggle is off in Settings → Dashboards while keeping native Lovelace reachable for editing.
data_description.sidebar_dashboards: Used when Top-level sidebar dashboards is set to "Selected dashboards".
data_description.default_dashboard: Optionally make one of the promoted Terrazzo dashboards Home Assistant's system default panel.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Terrazzo is already set up. Use Configure to change it.

data_description.title: The name of the /terrazzo panel in the sidebar.
data_description.dashboard: Leave empty to start on the dashboard picker.
data_description.top_level_dashboards: Show Lovelace dashboards directly in the sidebar as Terrazzo panels (/terrazzo-<slug>) and hide the generic Terrazzo link. Choose "Hidden Lovelace dashboards" to automatically promote dashboards whose "Show in sidebar" toggle is off in Settings → Dashboards while keeping native Lovelace reachable for editing.
data_description.sidebar_dashboards: Used when Top-level sidebar dashboards is set to "Selected dashboards".
data_description.default_dashboard: Optionally make one of the promoted Terrazzo dashboards Home Assistant's system default panel.
data_description.mcp_user: Off, or the one Home Assistant user an AI assistant may act as through /api/terrazzo/mcp, with that user's permissions on this instance only. Only that user's access tokens are accepted. Locks and alarm panels stay read-only.
data_description.agent: Empty, or the Home Assistant conversation agent that edits dashboards from the Terrazzo panel and apps: one of an AI integration's agents (OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic, Ollama, OpenRouter, …) with "Terrazzo dashboards" turned on among the APIs it may control, in that agent's own options. The apps then open a chat with it to edit a dashboard: it drafts changes as the person chatting, with their permissions, and they apply them.

yaml_overrides_ui.title: Terrazzo is configured in YAML
yaml_overrides_ui.description: Terrazzo's `terrazzo:` block in configuration.yaml is applied again on every start, so it replaces changes made under Settings → Devices & services. Your settings are already in the integration: remove the `terrazzo:` block and restart to manage Terrazzo from the UI.

web_origin.title: Allow Terrazzo at {origin} to load images

confirm.title: Allow {origin}?
confirm.description:
Terrazzo at {origin} is signed in to Home Assistant, but Home Assistant blocks it from loading camera and entity pictures. Allowing it adds {origin} to Home Assistant's allowed CORS origins, then restarts Home Assistant. Terrazzo confirms the change once Home Assistant is back; if it doesn't start, Home Assistant reverts it after five minutes.

Only allow a site you installed Terrazzo on yourself.

abort.unsupported: This Home Assistant keeps its HTTP settings in configuration.yaml. Add {origin} under `http:` → `cors_allowed_origins` and restart.
abort.not_running: Home Assistant is still starting. Try again once it has finished.
abort.pending_change: Another HTTP settings change is waiting to be confirmed. Confirm or discard it first.

agent_moved.title: Choose a conversation agent for Terrazzo's dashboard chat
agent_moved.description:
Terrazzo no longer calls {service} itself. Its dashboard chat is now answered by one of Home Assistant's own conversation agents, which keeps the key and the model, so the chat is off until you choose one. The saved key was removed from Terrazzo.

1. Add the {integration} integration under Settings → Devices & services, with your key, if you don't have it yet.
2. Add a conversation agent there (or open an existing agent's settings), pick a model that supports tool calling, and tick **Terrazzo dashboards** under its AI tools.
3. Open Terrazzo's settings (the link below) and choose that agent as the **Dashboard agent**.

This repair goes away once an agent is chosen.

agent_no_tools.title: Turn on Terrazzo dashboards for {agent}
agent_no_tools.description:
Terrazzo's dashboard chat uses {agent}, but that agent doesn't have **Terrazzo dashboards** turned on, so it can't read or draft dashboards and the chat can only say so.

Open {integration} (the link below), open the agent's settings (the cog beside it), tick **Terrazzo dashboards** under its AI tools, and submit. Or choose another agent in Terrazzo's settings.

This repair goes away the next time Terrazzo checks after the change: when the panel or an app opens, or the chat's next turn.
